title: Debugging conflicting styles in developer tools
learningObjectives: Use browser developer tools to locate matching CSS rules, identify overridden declarations, and make a targeted fix.

understand.concept: CSS debugging is the process of finding why an element looks different from the expected result. The Styles and Computed panels show matching declarations, overridden rules, inherited values and final computed values.
understand.whyItMatters: It helps you fix the actual cause instead of adding another override that makes the stylesheet more confusing.
understand.analogy: It is like tracing a result back through the instructions that produced it.
understand.analogyLimit: Developer tools show the browser's current document and computed styles. They do not automatically explain the design intention behind every rule.

explain.narrative: Right-click an element and choose Inspect. In Styles, find the rule that sets the property and look for crossed-out declarations; these are overridden in the current cascade. In Computed, inspect the final value and expand its source where available. Check selector match, specificity, origin/importance, layers and source order. Also check whether the element is inheriting a value, whether a media query is active, and whether a stylesheet loaded successfully.

practise.guidedTask: Open the preview, inspect the card, locate the crossed-out background declaration, and identify the winning selector.
practise.independentTask: Create a deliberate conflict between an element, class and ID selector. Use developer tools to record the winning rule and explain the result.
hints: Styles shows matched rules; Computed shows the final property value.
A crossed-out declaration is not necessarily invalid; it may simply lose the cascade.

questions.prompt: Which panel is best for checking the final computed property value?
questions.explanation: The Computed panel reports the final resolved property value.

questions.prompt: What does a crossed-out CSS declaration usually mean?
options: It is overridden in the current cascade
